pages.text: Three years on, I raised the altar beside the old tree at the heart of the village square.$(br2)With the $(item)Weather Altar Core$() as its heart, I planted a $(item)Tuning Pedestal$() on each of the four sides and let the veins in the stone join end to end - only then will the breath of the sky consent to follow the runes.

pages.title: They Call Me a God
pages.text: When the core settled upon the pedestal, the whole sky trembled softly in my palm.$(br2)The villagers fell to their knees and called me the Sky-Tuner.$(br2)I only smiled: I had simply invited the clouds to a place willing to listen to them.

pages.title: To Summon Wind and Rain
pages.text: Since then, holding the $(item)Tuning Chart$() and striking the core once unfolds a tuning diagram from my palm.$(br2)Draw upon it to call the clear sky, the rain, or the thunder - the weather bows its head and obeys a mortal's will.$(br2)(They insist it is a miracle. I still hold, stubbornly, that it is merely an equation not yet balanced.)
